segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He set out from there and went into the region of Judea and across the Jordan. Crowds again gathered around him, and, as was his custom, he again taught them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked him whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What did Moses command you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of dismissal and divorce her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But from the beginning of creation ‘he made them male and female.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two but one flesh.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the house the disciples asked him about this again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and if she divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: People were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let the children come to me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before him, and asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not give false testimony; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, I have kept all these since my youth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But his face fell at these words, and he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were utterly astounded and said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Then who can be saved?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “With people it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter began to say to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the sake of the good news

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: who will not receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Grant us to sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are able.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus called them to him and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones wield authority over them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But it is not so among you. Rather, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a sizable crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus stopped and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Call him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they called the blind man, saying to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Take courage! Get up; he is calling you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Throwing off his cloak, he jumped up and came to Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The blind man said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbouni, let me see again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go; your faith has saved you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately he could see again, and he followed him on the road.

notes.traditional: Pharisees came up and asked him
notes.note: Many manuscripts read “Pharisees came up and asked him,” as in the parallel at Matthew 19:3, and most English versions follow them. The SBLGNT follows the witnesses that leave the questioners unnamed, judging that “Pharisees” was brought in from Matthew.

The verb means to put someone to the test, here with a question meant to trap. Older versions have “tempting,” which now suggests enticement to sin; most modern translations also use “test” in this verse.

notes.phrase: and be united to his wife
notes.note: Some important early manuscripts lack these words, and some critical editions bracket them. They may have been added to complete the quotation of Genesis 2:24, or dropped by a copyist’s slip of the eye. The SBLGNT prints them without brackets.

In ordinary Jewish practice of the period only a husband could initiate a divorce, whereas Roman law allowed a wife to do so. Only Mark records this half of the saying. Many scholars think it applies Jesus’ teaching to the wider Greco-Roman setting of Mark’s readers, though this is not certain.

The Greek can mean “as a child receives it” or “as one receives a child.” Most interpreters and translations take the first sense, which the English word order here also suggests. The second would tie the saying to Jesus’ welcome of the children in this scene.

Unlike the rest of the list, this is not one of the Ten Commandments. The verb is used of withholding what is owed to someone, such as wages. It may stand in for the commandment against coveting or echo laws against cheating workers; Matthew and Luke do not include it in their parallels.

notes.phrase: how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God
notes.traditional: how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter the kingdom of God
notes.note: Many manuscripts add “for those who trust in riches,” and the King James Version follows them. The shorter reading, found in some of the earliest witnesses, makes the statement general. Most modern editions and translations adopt it.

The Greek was an ordinary word for an announcement of good news, used also of public and imperial proclamations. “Gospel” has since become a religious term and the name of a kind of book, so “good news” is used here. Many modern translations alternate between the two.

notes.phrase: in the age to come, eternal life
notes.note: “Eternal” translates an adjective formed from the word for “age” in the same sentence. In Jewish usage of the period, eternal life is the life of the coming age, set here against “this present time.” It describes the kind of life as well as its length, and “eternal” remains the standard rendering.

The verb is the ordinary Greek word for transferring someone into another’s custody, and it occurs twice in this verse: Jesus is handed over to the priests, who hand him over to the Gentiles. Older versions have “delivered,” and many use “betrayed” where Judas is in view. One rendering is kept here so that the chain of handings-over stays visible.

The Greek word means “nations” or “peoples”; in the plural, in Jewish usage, it regularly means the non-Jewish peoples. Here it refers in practice to the Roman authorities. The same word appears in verse 42.

In Israel’s Scriptures a cup is a common image for the lot God gives someone to undergo, often suffering or judgment. “Baptism” here is likewise a figure: the verb could be used of being plunged into or overwhelmed by calamity. Both images point to Jesus’ coming death.

The word was used for the price paid to free a slave or a captive, and in the Septuagint for payments that redeem a life or property. The preposition translated “for” commonly means “in place of” or “in exchange for.” How far the image should be pressed, and to whom any payment is made, is debated.

Mark gives the Aramaic word untranslated, and it is kept here as he has it. It is a heightened form of “Rabbi,” meaning “my master” or “my teacher”; John 20:16 glosses it as “Teacher.” Many English versions substitute “Rabbi” or “My teacher.”

The verb covers both rescue from illness or danger and salvation in the fuller sense. It is the same word the disciples use in verse 26 (“who can be saved?”). Most versions render “made you well” or “healed you” here; “saved” keeps the link, and many interpreters think Mark intends both senses.

candidates.reason: The verb means release, dismiss or send away as well as divorce, and versions vary between “divorce,” “put away” and “send away” in the marriage sayings across the Gospels.
In healing stories translators split between “save,” “heal” and “make well,” which hides the recurring formula “your faith has saved you” and its link to salvation language.
Versions vary between “slave,” “servant” and “bondservant,” and it must stay distinct from διάκονος throughout the New Testament.
It recurs throughout the Gospels and Acts and is rendered “scribes,” “teachers of the law” or “legal experts”; “scribe” may suggest a mere copyist to modern readers.
This Aramaic title, left untranslated in the Greek here and at John 20:16, needs one policy alongside ῥαββί on whether to keep the loanword or translate it.
